Lateral movement to two more engineers via internal AI tool
Use of stolen creds to deploy container and malicious script

summary: Binance said the $6.34 billion theft of October 29, 2026 was the end of a months-long campaign. In June an engineer on its wallet infrastructure team installed a tampered installer while setting up an AI coding tool, exposing team roles. In September another engineer was approached on a job-hunting platform by a fake Project Director, and in a second fake interview was told to run a coding assignment whose repository installed a backdoor on his work computer. On October 20 the attackers used that machine and an internal AI tool to compromise two more engineers, one with a container deployment token for the wallet signing service. On October 29 they used stolen credentials, deployed a container and ran a malicious script that drained Binance hot wallets across ten blockchains. The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor.
